sidebar.ahp_description: Defining weights manually can be subjective and inconsistent. The Analytic Hierarchy Process uses pairwise comparisons to mathematically derive optimal weights while measuring your decision consistency.
sidebar.dimension_weighting_note: Note: When all dimensions have equal weights you will get the "Political" IMPT. We do not recommended using it for decision making, as it assumes that all dimensions are equally important, which can mask inequalities. We reccomend the usage of AHP methodology to determine the weights that best suit your local context.

tutorial.prompt_tour: Would you like to take a quick tour of the dashboard?
tutorial.mobile_step_menu: On mobile, you can access the settings and indicators by tapping this menu button.
tutorial.step_1: Tutorial will be made available in a future update.
tutorial.step_2: Use the left sidebar to toggle the different layers.
tutorial.step_3: You can check the Mobility Poverty Index computed according to several criteria (and even compute one adapted to your local context, under IMPT dynamic).
tutorial.step_4: You can check the values computed for each aggregated dimension.
tutorial.step_5: And even analyse each individual metric that contributed to each of the dimensions.
tutorial.step_6: For each layer, you can apply global filters (such as travel modes or bounds).
tutorial.step_7: And see the data at different scales.
tutorial.step_8: Change the region to adapt the scale to different areas.
tutorial.step_9: Regional contrasts panel show you the 5 best and worst performers for the layer selected.
tutorial.step_10: When you click on the map, it is replaced by the area details.
tutorial.step_11: Refer to the scale for details on the metric you have selected.
tutorial.step_12: Use these controls to adapt the visualization to your needs.
tutorial.step_13: Finally, use these buttons to improve your experience.
tutorial.step_18: Find out more abut the project.
tutorial.step_10_mobile: Click any area on the map to see the details.
tutorial.dynamic_step_1: You can define your own weights for each dimension. Use these sliders to adjust how much each dimension contributes to your custom index.
tutorial.dynamic_step_1_note: Please mind this note before proceeding.
tutorial.dynamic_step_2: If you're not sure about the weights, take the AHP survey. It helps you derive consistent weights through simple pairwise comparisons.
tutorial.dynamic_step_3: Once you're satisfied with your custom index, you can download the results for all areas in a CSV file.
